title: Parade band personnel and the two tenors
summary: Bull lists the players in the parade band, and they discuss how two tenors worked without a clarinet and Manuel Paul's playing.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Jules Cahn took some photos and he also took a movie of some of it. Who was in the band, by the way? There was a fella called Brown on Tuba. I don't know his name. Little fella. William Grant. They just call him Brown. Manuel Paul and Andrew Morgan on tenors. Two tenors. No clarinet. I think Andrew Morgan was supposed to play clarinet. I think they expected him to, but he turned up with his tenor. So there were two tenors. Chicken Henry and Earl Humphrey. Booker T. And his son, Papa, I think, what's his name? Noel, isn't it?
Noel Glass. Noel was on snare and Booker T. On bass drum. Then there was myself, Sheik and Peter Boccage and this fella, Baptiste, on trumpet.
How did the two tenors work together?

Two tenors sounded alright. Sounded quite good. I think it would have been better if there had been a clarinet in there because there was, you know, there was sort of no great contrast in there. But they sounded quite good. Adrian Morgan played pretty well. Is Manuel Paul any good? Manuel Paul's genius, yeah. He's one of my favourite musicians in the city, I think. Amongst about ten or fifteen others. But he is, you know, he's excellent, I think.
